lesson.title: Review Day: The Legacies of Colonialism
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: This week you traced colonialism's lasting legacies. Let's review it all!

Quick review: independence movements sought self-governance worldwide (Day 1). Colonial-era borders often ignored existing cultural/religious lines, creating lasting challenges (Day 2). Economic legacies left many former colonies dependent on narrow raw-material exports (Day 3). Cultural legacies, like language, could be both an advantage and a loss (Day 4). Write a short paragraph explaining how these four legacies connect to form one bigger picture of colonialism's lasting impact on the modern world.

Great work this week — you traced colonialism's lasting legacies across politics, economics, and culture! A future unit will study the 1947 partition of India and Pakistan as one specific, historically significant case connected to this week's border-challenge pattern, treated with the depth and care it deserves.

objectives: Review independence movements, colonial borders, economic legacies, and cultural legacies
Write a short paragraph connecting all four legacies into one coherent picture
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child write their connecting paragraph.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of colonialism's legacies, and note that a future unit will study the partition of India as a specific, carefully-sourced case study.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two of the four legacies the child remembers best rather than requiring all four in the paragraph
Ready for more: ask the child which of the four legacies they think has the most lasting effect on the world today, and why
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four colonialism-legacy topics needs the most reinforcement going forward, and re-affirms the deliberate deferral of partition-specific content
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended synthesis activity — check that the paragraph connects at least two or three of the week's legacies into a coherent picture, for example noting that colonial borders and economic structures together often shaped which newly independent nations faced the greatest post-independence challenges, while cultural legacies like language continue to shape daily life in complex ways today.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's WA Social Studies and C3 Framework History/Economics/Culture standards on colonialism's legacies before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session, and explicitly re-affirms the deliberate deferral of the 1947 partition to a future, dedicated unit.
